selection_metadata.provider_regression_guard: Each provider validation normalized MAE may worsen no more than 2% versus seasonal naive; select smallest qualified provider-balanced normalized MAE
selection_metadata.validation_target: Provider-specific geographic and terminal-time validation; Uzbekistan January-December 2025 is legacy development validation
selection_metadata.test_protocol: Fresh independent international geographic plus terminal-year holdout is constructed explicitly only after model freeze; previous Uzbekistan and synthetic test outcomes are legacy regression benchmarks.
selection_metadata.selection_metric: Provider-balanced macro per-history-normalized validation MAE; training loss weight equal by provider; no final test outcomes used

abs.grouping: Provider-prefixed state/province; all industry series from one geography stay together. Sector records are dependent aggregate series, not independent firms.
abs.split_algorithm: SHA256('international-region-v1:' + provider + ':' + geography), sorted; floor(0.6*n) train, half remaining validation/test
abs.quality_policy: Reject an entire case if any required history/target month is missing, suppressed, unreliable, nonfinite or negative. Published zero sales remain actual zeros; all-zero history is excluded.
abs.test_policy: Terminal test labels are imported but must not be read for training or validation selection; build test cases only after final model freeze.

statcan.quality_policy: Reject an entire case if any required history/target month is missing, suppressed, unreliable, nonfinite or negative. Published zero sales remain actual zeros; all-zero history is excluded.
statcan.test_policy: Terminal test labels are imported but must not be read for training or validation selection; build test cases only after final model freeze.

selection_metadata.temporal_scope: Holdouts are provider-local terminal years; Uzbekistan training through December 2025 overlaps some Australian/Canadian holdout dates. No absolute year, provider identity or cross-country shock covariates are features; this is not a globally chronological unseen-future test.
selection_metadata.limitations: Original retail turnover and service value are aggregate revenue proxies, not independent firm cash receipts. Native currency units remain separate and only dimensionless errors are pooled. Survey revisions, correlated economic shocks, Uzbekistan short post-methodology histories, and cross-country aggregate-to-borrower transfer limit claims. No real costs, defaults or repayments are supplied.

predetermined_acceptance.policy: Engineering guardrail: positive overall macro historical-scale-normalized MAE improvement against fixed seasonal naive, and no provider more than 10% worse. Cluster uncertainty is reported rather than hidden. This is not validation of individual borrowers, loan repayment, calibrated confidence or default risk.

metric_policy: Primary comparisons use historical-scale-normalized absolute error. Raw MAE and WAPE are computed within each provider's declared units only, never pooled across AUD/CAD. sMAPE assigns exactly zero error to actual=forecast=0; all other observations are included. Seasonal MASE divides by mean absolute 12-month differences in the input history only, with undefined short or constant histories reported. WAPE includes zero and near-zero months; an all-zero actual denominator is undefined.
test_policy: Final labels are used only by this evaluator after model candidate and transfer selection are frozen. Fixed seasonal naive is the comparison, not another selected candidate. No fitting, tuning or selection occurs here. Previously inspected Uzbekistan and synthetic tests are separate legacy regression benchmarks.
scope: Licensed real aggregate revenue only. No real borrower expense, payment-capacity, repayment or default outcomes are available. This forecast evaluation does not validate lending decisions.
limitations: All sectors of a geography share an entity group. Related sectors and regions remain correlated through national economic shocks; clustered intervals from the small number of final geographies are descriptive. Time boundaries are provider-specific: other countries can have training observations later than an international test date, so this is not a globally chronological future holdout. Provider snapshots use one current revision vintage, not unrevised observations available at each historical date. International aggregate turnover can differ materially from an individual borrower's bank receipts.
